## Loading libraries

```{r}
#| message: false

library("tidyverse")
```

## Loading the data

```{r}
laml_metadata <- read_tsv(
  file = "../data/01_dat_load_meta.tsv.gz"
)

laml_expression <- read_tsv(
  file = "../data/01_dat_load_expr.tsv.gz"
)
```

## Data wrangling

### Checking gene identifiers

Check the completeness and uniqueness of gene identifiers before reshaping the expression data.

```{r}
laml_expression |>
  summarise(
    total_rows = n(),
    unique_gene_ids = n_distinct(Ensembl_ID),
    missing_gene_ids = sum(is.na(Ensembl_ID))
  )
```

All 60,660 gene identifiers are unique and non-missing. No gene identifier cleaning is required.

### Checking and matching samples

#### Checking for duplicate sample identifiers

```{r}
# Count how many times each sample ID occurs
laml_metadata |>
  count(sample,
        sort = TRUE) |>
  filter(n > 1)
```

```{r}
laml_metadata |>
  summarise(
    metadata_rows = n(),
    unique_samples = n_distinct(sample),
    unique_patients = n_distinct(submitter_id)
  )
```

The metadata contains 278 unique samples from 200 patients. Multiple samples can originate from the same patient; therefore, we retain all sample-level records before matching.

#### Checking missing values and gender distribution

```{r}
# Count missing values in selected metadata columns
laml_metadata |>
  summarise(
    missing_gender = sum(is.na(gender.demographic)),
    missing_age = sum(is.na(age_at_index.demographic)),
    missing_sample = sum(is.na(sample)),
    missing_patient = sum(is.na(submitter_id))
  )
```

```{r}
# Count metadata records in each gender category
laml_metadata |>
  count(gender.demographic,
        sort = TRUE)
```

There are no missing values in the gender, age, sample and patient identifier columns. The metadata contains 150 male and 128 female records. \#### Matching metadata to expression samples

```{r}
# Extract sample identifiers from the expression dataset
expression_samples <- laml_expression |>
  select(-Ensembl_ID) |>
  names() |>
  tibble(sample = _)
```

```{r}
expression_samples |>
  anti_join(laml_metadata,
            by = "sample") |>
  count(name = "missing_metadata")
```

```{r}
laml_metadata |>
  anti_join(expression_samples,
            by = "sample") |>
  count(name = "unmatched_metadata")
```

All expression samples have corresponding metadata. However, 127 metadata records have no corresponding expression measurements and are excluded from the matched dataset.

```{r}
# Keep metadata records for samples present in the expression matrix
laml_metadata_matched <- laml_metadata |>
  semi_join(expression_samples,
            by = "sample")
```

```{r}
# Check the number of samples and patients in the matched metadata
laml_metadata_matched |>
  summarise(
    metadata_rows = n(),
    unique_samples = n_distinct(sample),
    unique_patients = n_distinct(submitter_id)
  )
```

```{r}
# Count gender categories among samples in the expression matrix
laml_metadata_matched |>
  count(gender.demographic,
        sort = TRUE)
```

After matching, 151 samples from 151 unique patients remain, comprising 84 male and 67 female patients. Each patient contributes one expression sample.

### Reshaping expression data

The expression dataset is organised in a wide format, where each row represents a gene and each sample has its own column. To prepare the data for subsequent analysis, we reshape the expression data into a long format and combine it with the corresponding patient metadata.

#### Testing the reshaping and metadata join on a subset

Test the reshaping and metadata join on a subset of ten genes before applying the procedure to the complete dataset.

```{r}
# Select the first 10 genes to test the reshaping
laml_expression_test <- laml_expression |>
  slice_head(n = 10)
```

```{r}
# Reshape the expression data from wide to long format
laml_expression_test_long <- laml_expression_test |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Ensembl_ID,
    names_to = "sample",
    values_to = "expression"
  )

# Inspect the reshaped expression data
glimpse(laml_expression_test_long)

# Check the number of rows and columns
dim(laml_expression_test_long)
```

```{r}
# Add gender information to the expression data
laml_expression_test_joined <- laml_expression_test_long |>
  left_join(
    laml_metadata_matched |>
      select(sample,
             gender.demographic),
    by = "sample"
  )

# Inspect the joined dataset
glimpse(laml_expression_test_joined)
```

```{r}
# Count observations in each gender category
laml_expression_test_joined |>
  count(gender.demographic,
        sort = TRUE)

# Check for missing gender information after joining
laml_expression_test_joined |>
  summarise(
    missing_gender = sum(is.na(gender.demographic))
  )
```

The test produces 1,510 gene–sample observations with no missing gender information, confirming that the reshaping and joining procedures work as intended.

#### Reshaping the complete dataset

We apply the same transformation to the complete expression dataset.

```{r}
# Reshape the complete expression dataset into long format
laml_expression_long <- laml_expression |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Ensembl_ID,
    names_to = "sample",
    values_to = "expression"
  )
```

```{r}
# Inspect the reshaped expression dataset
glimpse(laml_expression_long)

# Check the dimensions
dim(laml_expression_long)
```

The reshaped dataset contains 9,159,660 observations, corresponding to 60,660 genes measured across 151 samples.

### Combining expression data with metadata

After reshaping the expression data, we combine it with the matched metadata using the sample identifier.

```{r}
# Add gender information to the complete expression dataset
laml_expression_joined <- laml_expression_long |>
  left_join(
    laml_metadata_matched |>
      select(sample,
             gender.demographic),
    by = "sample"
  )
```

```{r}
# Check the joined dataset
laml_expression_joined |>
  summarise(
    total_rows = n(),
    unique_genes = n_distinct(Ensembl_ID),
    unique_samples = n_distinct(sample),
    missing_expression = sum(is.na(expression)),
    infinite_expression = sum(is.infinite(expression)),
    duplicate_gene_sample = n() - n_distinct(Ensembl_ID,
                                             sample),
    missing_gender = sum(is.na(gender.demographic))
  )
```

```{r}
# Count expression observations by gender
laml_expression_joined |>
  count(gender.demographic,
        sort = TRUE)
```

The final dataset contains 9,159,660 gene–sample observations across 60,660 genes and 151 samples. No missing or infinite expression values, duplicate gene–sample combinations or missing gender information were detected. The cleaned dataset is ready for downstream analysis.

## Saving cleaned data

Save the matched metadata and tidy expression dataset as compressed TSV files for downstream analysis.

```{r}
# Save the matched metadata
write_tsv(
  laml_metadata_matched,
  file = "../data/02_dat_clean_meta.tsv.gz"
)

# Save the joined gene expression data
write_tsv(
  laml_expression_joined,
  file = "../data/02_dat_clean_expr.tsv.gz"
)
```
